newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU rejects demands for higher malt export refund.
newsitem.headline: EU rejects demands for higher malt export refund.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday rebuffed attempts by the food industry to get an increase in export subsidies for malt by decising to keep the current refund unchanged, member country officials said.
The standing export refund for unroasted malt remains at 32.50 Ecus per tonne, they said after weekly grain talks in Brussels.
The European Commission was unavailable for comment.

But export sources who track EU policy said the Commission was unwilling to raise the refund because it believed European malt was competitive and an increase would only help brewing firms in wealthy countries lap up cheap supplies.
"We have the cheapest malt in the world. If we put up the refund it is only going to help the Japanese brewers," said one source who supports the EU decision.
European malting supplies are plentiful and cheap this year because of a large harvest of barley, the sources said.
Further, malt firms have already taken up refunds at the existing level to export around 10 percent of their annual flow of two million tonnes, they said.
The malt export refund is at the centre of an escalating row between the Commission and malt firms who want the subsidy up.

They say the current refund is unfair when compared to export subsidies for barley. Malt subsidies are often set 30 percent above the barley refund but are currently only five percent above the latest barley subsidy of 30.95 Ecus per tonne.
Malting firms declined to comment on Thursday's decision and their industry representatives were unavailable for comment.
